items.basis: The claimed multidirectional flow improvement through asymmetric octant modification lacks fluid dynamics validation; the candidate provides no CFD simulations or experimental data demonstrating that the modified Schwarz P unit cell actually creates the claimed multidirectional flow pattern that would disrupt biofilm formation.

The boundary condition of chloride concentrations below 0.5 ppm is unrealistically strict for district cooling systems; typical district cooling water contains 50-200 ppm chlorides, violating the claimed safe operating conditions and making the invention impractical for real-world implementation.

The candidate's own evidence [doi:10.3323/jcorr1974.29.7_354] demonstrates that stainless steel 316L is susceptible to stress corrosion cracking in chloride environments, directly contradicting the claimed boundary condition of safe operation at the required low chloride concentrations.

The asymmetric octant segment geometry would require complex manufacturing processes that are incompatible with standard plate heat exchanger production methods, which rely on symmetrical designs for efficient stamping and welding processes.

The testable prediction fails to specify the exact temperature differentials, water quality parameters beyond chloride, and cleaning protocols that would be used to validate the claimed performance, introducing multiple variables that could explain results.
